summary.en: A nonzero condition chooses the first alternative.
summary.bn: condition ? a : b দিয়ে একটি মান বেছে নাও এবং বড় expression ছোট ধাপে ভাঙো।

notes: The conditional operator is available in C89 through C23. These examples use its C17 arithmetic and pointer rules. The chosen operand alone is evaluated, but both operand types participate in determining the result type.

examples.title: Choose a larger mark
examples.explanationHtml: Seventy exceeds eighty-five is false. The expression selects b, so maximum becomes eighty-five. The comparison itself does not change either mark. The chosen value is stored before it is printed.

examples.title: Skip zero division
examples.explanationHtml: The false condition chooses the fallback zero. The division alternative is not evaluated, so a zero divisor is never used. A real application should choose a fallback meaningfully; zero average and no data may need different labels.

examples.title: Maximum of three scores
examples.explanationHtml: The first comparison selects ninety-one from the first pair. The second compares that candidate with the third score, also ninety-one. Choosing either tied value gives the same numeric maximum. A separate winner label would require a tie rule.

practice.title: Minimum of two
practice.statementHtml: Read a and b from -100 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print the smaller value and newline.

practice.title: Pass label
practice.statementHtml: Read mark 0 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print Pass for mark at least 40, otherwise Fail; end the line.

practice.title: Safe whole quotient
practice.statementHtml: Read total 0 to 100 and count 0 to 10. After the prompt Input: , print total / count when count is nonzero, otherwise -1; end the line.
hints: Put division only in the nonzero alternative.

practice.title: Maximum of three rolls
practice.statementHtml: Read a, b and c from 0 to 9999. After the prompt Input: , print their maximum and newline using two conditional expressions.
hints: Keep the best value seen so far.

quiz.explanation: The condition and two alternatives are its three operands.

quiz.prompt: Which alternative follows a zero condition?
options: The expression before the question mark

quiz.prompt: How do nested conditional expressions associate?
quiz.explanation: Explicit parentheses can make the grouping clearer.

quiz.prompt: Which design is clearest for finding a maximum of three beginners can trace?
options: Compare a pair, then compare its winner with the third
quiz.explanation: Two named steps expose the candidate value.

quiz.prompt: What happens to an int and double pair of arithmetic alternatives?
options: The condition selects a type at runtime
A common arithmetic type is determined
quiz.explanation: Both operand types participate even though only one value is evaluated.

quiz.prompt: When is if-else usually clearer than ?:?
options: When a choice needs several statements
quiz.explanation: A statement block better expresses several actions.

quiz.prompt: A false greater-than condition chooses which mark?
A negative condition is nonzero. Which label appears?
quiz.explanation: Negative two is true in a scalar condition.

quiz.prompt: An integer alternative shares an expression with double. How is the result displayed?
quiz.explanation: The arithmetic result type is double, so selected two prints as 2.0.

keyPoints.en: A nonzero condition chooses the first alternative.
keyPoints.bn: শর্ত nonzero হলে ?-এর পরের মানটি নেওয়া হয়।

keyPoints.en: A zero condition chooses the second alternative.
keyPoints.bn: শর্ত ০ হলে colon-এর পরের মানটি নেওয়া হয়।

keyPoints.en: Only the selected alternative is evaluated.
Two steps can find the maximum of three values.
keyPoints.bn: দুই ধাপে তিন সংখ্যার সর্বোচ্চ মান বের করা যায়।
অনেকগুলো ?: এক লাইনে গুঁজে না দিয়ে ছোট ধাপ লেখো।

examQuestions.question: How many operands does ?: have?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Three. The condition and two alternatives are its three operands.

examQuestions.question: Which alternative follows a zero condition?
examQuestions.answerHtml: The expression after the colon. Zero is false.

examQuestions.question: Read a, b and c from 0 to 9999. After Input: print their maximum and newline using two conditional expressions.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int a, b, c;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%d %d %d", &a, &b, &c) != 3 || a < 0 || a > 9999 || b < 0 || b > 9999 || c < 0 || c > 9999) {
        return 1;
    }
    int best = a > b ? a : b;
    best = best > c ? best : c;
    printf("%d\n", best);
    return 0;
}

Keep the best value seen so far.
